title: Seven layers of a Moriarty Web
intro: Proving Nothing describes every zero-knowledge system through seven layers: interdependent concerns, not seven runtime phases that execute in order. Read through them, a Moriarty Web is one system: financial rules become constraints, a private witness satisfies them, Groth16 seals a proof for each Strand, and a Cardano consumer accepts the transition only when every required Strand matches the transaction it settles.

layers.name: Setup
layers.headline: Keys made for one compiled relation
layers.body: Groth16 derives proving and verifying keys from secret randomness for one compiled circuit. Each distinct compiled relation needs its own setup; the count follows circuits, not predicates or catalogue entries. Whoever keeps that randomness can forge proofs, so soundness assumes it is destroyed.
layers.mapping: Catalogue entries and owner intents name the verifying key.

layers.name: Language
layers.headline: Financial rules written as a program
layers.body: Moriarty programs state what an action may do: payment arithmetic, fees kept separate from repayment, caps an owner signs, and duties that continue. The compiler turns that source into constraints; a rule left unconstrained is a rule no proof enforces.
layers.mapping: Moriarty rules for payments, fees, caps and duties.

layers.name: Witness
layers.headline: Every step, recorded by the prover
layers.body: The prover runs the program over its inputs and records every intermediate value. Zero-knowledge keeps this assignment hidden, but only the assignment: amounts that appear in Cardano outputs or in the statement stay public. Witness generation must not leak values through its own behavior.
layers.mapping: One whole-execution witness can serve several Strand roles.

layers.name: Arithmetization
layers.headline: Every rule becomes an equation
layers.body: The compiled program becomes rank-1 constraints over a prime field, which Groth16 encodes as a quadratic arithmetic program. A valid witness satisfies every constraint. The public inputs carry a statement digest; an in-circuit BLAKE2b gadget ties them to the statement bytes.
layers.mapping: Caps, fees and duty updates become constraints.

layers.name: Proof System
layers.headline: A short certificate of correct computation
layers.body: Groth16 turns the witness into a constant-size proof checked by one pairing equation. Under an honest setup, knowledge soundness means a verifying proof shows the prover knew a satisfying witness; zero-knowledge means the proof reveals nothing beyond its statement. It never shows the statement's values describe the real ledger.

layers.name: Cryptographic Bedrock
layers.headline: Hard problems underneath
layers.body: A pairing-friendly elliptic curve supplies Groth16's groups and scalar field; Groth16's soundness argument holds in the generic bilinear group model. BLAKE2b collision resistance binds statement bytes to digests. Signatures authenticate owner intents and claimant releases. These primitives support the proof core and fix what it can express.
layers.mapping: Cardano scripts evaluate the pairing check and hashes.

layers.name: Verification
layers.headline: Proof meets ledger
layers.body: A claim policy checks each Groth16 proof and mints a proof-claim output. One settlement transaction consumes every Strand the Web requires; the validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and spent state, requires claimant signatures and enforces signed caps. Outside facts need a named issuer, authentication path and freshness limit.

relationshipsTitle: How the layers lean on each other
relationships: Layers 4, 5 and 6 form the proof core: the scalar field, the R1CS encoding and Groth16's pairing check are chosen as one design, not three.
Setup follows the compiled relation. Changing a rule changes the circuit, and a changed circuit needs a new setup and a new verifying key.
The proof and the ledger divide the work. Layers 3 to 5 show the statement's arithmetic is correct; Layer 7 checks, from the transaction itself, that the statement describes this step.
The verifier reaches down. Cardano scripts must run the pairing check, which constrains the curve and proof system beneath them.
The numbering follows how a reader meets the system, not the order of engineering decisions; the dependency lists here sketch the main pressures, not a complete graph.
mappingTitle: From book layer to Moriarty Web
credit: The seven-layer framework comes from Proving Nothing, cited at a pinned commit. The book explains zero-knowledge systems in general; the Moriarty mappings on this page are ours, not the book's.
